commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot to Proton and add greeting
implement mark as done without using additional class
Add unmark command without using additional classes
Refactor task data into a dedicated Task class

commitResults.messageBody:
The Java classes use the default package and leave parts of their public
API undocumented. Fixed values are also represented as mutable local
variables, including a misspelled separator name.

Move both classes into the proton package and document their public
APIs. Promote fixed values to named constants. This aligns the code with
the required se-edu conventions without changing chatbot behavior.

Terminal diffs are hard to navigate for large or multi-file changes.

Add a repository-scoped skill that generates a self-contained split-view
HTML comparison for commits and worktree changes. This gives reviewers
an interactive view without adding dependencies to the Java application.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add se-edu Java coding standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Java contributions need a consistent project-wide style reference.

Add a repository-scoped skill summarizing the se-edu basic and
intermediate Java conventions. Mandate it in AGENTS.md so future Java
changes are reviewed and validated against the same rules.

Commit messages need consistent structure and rationale.

Add a repository-scoped skill covering the se-edu commit and branch
conventions. Mandate it in AGENTS.md while preserving the existing
lightweight-tag and commit authorization rules.

Add the project-specific test-ui skill and initial UI test plan.

Compare exact outputs, stop on failure, and retain session transcripts.

Require agents to invoke the skill after every code change.

Recognize the todo command and show ToDo tasks with a T type marker.
Store task types as data to avoid introducing an inheritance hierarchy.
Add a console UI test for creating, listing, marking, and unmarking.

Recognize the deadline command and retain its /by value as text.
Display deadline tasks with a D marker and their due date or time.
Extend console UI coverage without introducing task inheritance.

Recognize the event command and retain its /from and /to values.
Display event tasks with an E marker and their start and end times.
Extend console UI coverage without introducing task inheritance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor task types to use inheritance
commitResults.messageBody:
Move shared description and completion behavior into Task.
Represent Todo, Deadline, and Event as specialized Task subclasses.
Keep task storage polymorphic while preserving console behavior.
Update the UI test build configuration for the new classes.

The entry point mixes startup, dispatch, parsing, and task operations.

Separate these concerns so each method stays focused.

The command chain nests every alternative under the preceding branch.

Use guard returns so readers can consider each command independently.

Mark and unmark duplicate parsing, bounds checks, and error handling.

Share that logic so both commands apply the same validation rules.

Typed task handlers repeat storage, counting, and confirmation output.

Use one workflow so every typed task is added consistently.

Parser keywords and delimiters are embedded as unexplained strings.

Name them so recognition and parsing share one command grammar.

The parser indexes fields that malformed commands may not contain.

Validate required fields so Proton reports the format and keeps running.

The fallback treats every unrecognized input as an untyped task.

Report unknown commands so the default branch has one clear meaning.

The comments only repeat information expressed by clear field names.

Keep comments focused on behavior and rationale that code cannot convey.

Add a Proton-specific checked exception at the command boundary.

Use positive-charge feedback for blank and unrecognized commands.

Reject empty todos and malformed deadline or event details with ProtonException.

Provide positive-charge guidance and UI coverage for each invalid command.

Handle missing, non-numeric, empty-list, and out-of-range task numbers with ProtonException.

Keep Proton running with positive-charge guidance and matching UI coverage.

Reject new tasks with ProtonException before the fixed task array reaches an invalid index.

Confirm the 100-task boundary and recovery behavior through the console UI plan.
Group task classes under proton.task and place the application exception under proton.exception. Keep the entry point in proton and update references to match the new structure.

Task storage uses a fixed array and a separate task counter,
limiting the list to 100 tasks.

Replace the array with an ArrayList<Task> and use its size for
task counts and bounds checks. Remove the fixed capacity limit
so the list can grow as tasks are added.

Update UI coverage to verify growth beyond 100 tasks and preserve
existing task creation, listing, marking, and unmarking behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for deleting tasks by number
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can add and update tasks but cannot remove them.

Support delete TASK_NUMBER using the task numbers shown by list.
Remove the selected task and display its details and the remaining
task count, following the required deletion output.

Reuse task-number validation for missing, invalid, and out-of-range
arguments. Add UI coverage for deletion, renumbering, and errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save tasks automatically after each list change
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks exist only in memory and are lost when Proton exits.

Write the full task list to data/proton.txt after additions,
completion changes, and deletions. Create the data directory
when needed and exclude saved tasks from version control.

Document the write-only behavior and add repeatable UI tests
that verify saved contents immediately after each change.
Defer loading saved tasks to a later implementation.

Validate all 13 UI cases with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load saved tasks when Proton starts
commitResults.messageBody:
Saved tasks are written to disk but are not restored on startup.

Restore task types, completion status, and details from the existing
UTF-8 save format before processing commands. Treat a missing file
as an empty list and stop on loading errors to preserve saved data.

Add UI coverage for loaded-task changes, empty and malformed files,
and persistence across restarts. Document the file format limits.

Validate all 16 UI cases with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Protect task data against storage failures
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving can truncate the previous file, and failed writes leave the
in-memory list changed. Display-based records also have ambiguous
field boundaries.

Replace saves atomically and restore the list when a command cannot
be saved. Detect external file changes before replacement and reject
malformed records without modifying the saved data.

Use versioned records with encoded UTF-8 fields while accepting valid
legacy saves. Reject control characters and validate task numbers
before converting them to zero-based indices.

Add console coverage for corrupted data, failed-save recovery,
external edits, Unicode, legacy migration, and end of input.

Validate all 39 UI cases with Java 25.
